name: Madder Violet
lede: Madder Violet is a deep, reddish purple named for the dye plant that gives madder red, and a color that old dyers and color chartmakers recognized as one of madder's side effects.

sections.title: A dye plant's violet
sections.body:
The name belongs to a color chart tradition: Ridgway listed Madder Violet in 1912 (plate XXV), Maerz and Paul recorded it the same year, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 placed it in block 224 [1]. The swatch here comes from a scan of an aged printed plate, so treat it as approximate [1]. The nearest named color in our library is [[byzantium]], about 10.6 units away, and a near-duplicate, Nigrosin Violet, sits only 1.8 units off [1].

The colour is deeper and quieter than the [[purple]] of a pure violet dye. Next to [[madder-lake]], the red it comes from, it is far darker.

sections.title: How madder makes violet
sections.body:
Madder is best known for red, but the dye bath yields other colors when the metal salt changes [2]. Writing in 1895, Cremer reported that adding iron sulfate to a madder lake gave a black-violet and a madder violet [2]. The Pigment Compendium adds a warning: madder lakes depend on so many variables that they are hard to replicate from recipes, and the work is more art than science [2].

Finlay tells the modern end of the story. In 1976 a German chemistry teacher, Harald Boehmer, began reviving natural dyes for carpets in Turkey, and in time found a way to make madder violet, which he kept as a trade secret for years [3]. The cooperative he and his wife founded, DoBAG, employed about a hundred weavers twenty years on [3]. The red they started from is the subject of [[madder]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units that covers at least five per cent of the canvas turns up in 11 works [4]. Five of them fall in the 1890s, a rate of about nine times the archive average for that decade [4]. The largest share belongs to Achille Laugé's 1893 portrait of a fair-haired girl, where it covers about 27 per cent [4]. About two-thirds of the matching area sits in shadows [4]. As photographed: museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings; a color match is not a pigment test.

questions.q: What does iron sulfate do to a madder lake, according to Cremer (1895)?
choices: Gives a black-violet and madder violet
questions.answer: Gives a black-violet and madder violet

questions.q: True or false: madder gives only red.

openers: Madder is not only red: with iron in the bath it can be pushed to violet.
Look at old dyed textiles for dark violet next to madder red; both can come from one plant.
